Home
A warm, family environment and community-driven ethos
Visit Us to Learn More
Delivering an excellent education since 1918
Visit Us to Learn More
Empowering our pupils with skills to navigate the world around them
Visit Us to Learn More
Established in 1918, Boundary Oak is a co-educational day and boarding school for pupils aged 2-16. Here, at our Hampshire home, you will find a culture of kindness, strong values, high standards and a wealth of opportunity. We believe in the power of individual potential.
Our play-based Early Years Foundation Stage makes early learning fun, brimming with activities and outdoor adventures.
Children engage in inspiring lessons with core and subject-specialist teachers who bring learning alive.
Pupils enjoy a busy, enriching school life full of experiences that help them to grow and build pathways to the future.
International, military and UK-based boarders join our cosy boarding family and welcoming school community.
We are a warm, welcoming independent day and boarding school with a broad, balanced curriculum. Our passionate teachers empower pupils to excel academically, build resilience and embrace opportunities, ensuring they thrive in school and leave us equipped with the skills to succeed in life.
Education at Boundary Oak is rooted in cultivating well-rounded individuals who will thrive academically and personally.
Our warm and welcoming environment provides exceptional individualised care, so pupils feel happy and in the mindset to achieve their goals.
Our pupils broaden their horizons and gain life skills through plentiful opportunities to participate in sports, co-curricular activities, outdoor learning, inter-school competitions, and international events.
Our pupils graduate with strong academic results and varied skills, securing places at excellent onward destinations, prepared for life, and ready to contribute as global citizens.
Boundary Oak School Achieves Platinum Woodland Trust Green Tree Award.
One such example is Oliver, the Head Boy from the Class of 2024, whose passion for academics and athletics has shaped his journey.
Visiting in person is the best way to experience our homely atmosphere and day-to-day life here.
We aim to make our admissions process as smooth as possible for our prospective families.
Join one of our upcoming Open Days.

Children aged 4+ can join our Breakfast Club from 07:40.
Flexible afterschool care is available for Reception pupils and is free of charge until 16:30 to enable simultaneous sibling pick-up with older siblings. From 16:30, after school care is charged at £3.00 per 30 minutes.
All children from Reception onwards are welcome to stay for Big Tea (dinner), where they will enjoy a freshly cooked evening meal with our boarders.
Bookings are handled via the School Office.
Breakfast Club (07:40 to 08:15)
After school care (15:30 to 18:00)
Big Tea (17:30 to 18:30)

Our Careers Programme
Career education supports pupils in making informed decisions for the future.
Our carefully planned programme includes PSHE lessons, form time, assemblies and career focus days. We provide personalised opportunities to develop pupils’ employability skills, including problem-solving, communication, critical thinking, risk-taking, creativity, leadership and teamwork. Visits from Teck Trucks and guest speakers from diverse sectors alongside trips to university conferences, aviation simulators, and Sky Studios, broaden pupils' exposure to various industries, helping them explore the full range of opportunities available to them. We encourage all pupils to follow their passions, make good choices, and develop the skills to lead them into their chosen careers.
Senior careers journey
In our Senior School, our pupils use Unifrog, a high-quality careers platform that provides assessments and guidance resources. Our pupils also receive a range of career opportunities such as:
Our Beyond Boundary Oak event, which sees all local colleges and sixth forms come to the school to speak to our Year 10 pupils and parents
Information, advice and guidance, and group career sessions from neighbouring sixth forms
Mentoring and coaching from Morrisby advisors and staff
A careers hot-desking event with networking opportunities
Workplace visits, work experience placements, and work taster events
Access to open days at further and higher education institutions, plus training and apprenticeship providers
A 1:1 careers information advice and guidance interview
An Interview preparation day and an employer interview day
Help with CVs, job searches and interviews

Academic results and destinations
Our Senior pupils consistently achieve +1 value-added grades across all subjects over the national average.
These exceptional results are a testament to the dedication and collaboration between our teachers and pupils, working together to unlock and reach each pupil's full potential.
Recent results
97% Overall Pass Rate
40% of pupils secured Grade 7 or higher (A/A*).
1/3 of pupils achieved exceptional value-added scores, gaining an average of +2 grades per subject compared to their baseline assessment.
100% of pupils in Further Mathematics secured Grade 7 or higher (A/A*) alongside 80% of Triple Science pupils.
In Geography, History, Business Studies, French and Music, at least 60% of pupils also attained at least a Grade 7.
Building Strong Foundations for GCSE Success
GCSE success at Boundary Oak is built over time, starting with the strong academic foundations established in our Junior School.
Bonnie joined Boundary Oak in Reception and went on to achieve 10 GCSEs awarded at Grade 9. Mason, a military boarder and a pupil since Year 3, achieved an average +2.5 grade gain across all his subjects. With both securing their Sixth Form of choice, these results demonstrate the strength of our Boarding provision and whole-school approach in preparing pupils to excel at GCSE and beyond.
Mrs Savage reflects:
“I am absolutely delighted with the results they have achieved. These outcomes reflect not only their academic ability, but also the dedication, perseverance and positive attitude they have demonstrated throughout their time at Boundary Oak School.
This year group has been a genuine pleasure to work with. Over the past few years, we have watched them mature into confident, thoughtful and responsible young people who have embraced every opportunity available to them. Their exceptional work ethic, commitment to their studies and willingness to support one another have been evident throughout their GCSE journey, and they thoroughly deserve this success."
A-Levels and beyond
Our pupils progress to a wide range of schools and colleges across England.
Over the last five years, some of the highlight destination schools include:

Pastoral Care
Nurture is our foundation. Our caring family community values, supports and respects every pupil's wellbeing.
A note from our Head of Pastoral Care
Boundary Oak is committed to nurturing every child's emotional and physical well-being through a thoughtful, holistic approach. Our dedicated pastoral team, supported by all staff, ensures that every pupil feels safe, respected, and valued, with access to help whenever needed.
The culture at Boundary Oak encourages strong relationships between staff and pupils, enabling early identification and resolution of any concerns.
We believe passionately in the importance of listening to our pupils. Their opinions and ideas are gathered through the School Council, suggestion boxes, pupil surveys, and our dedicated pastoral website. This platform allows pupils to communicate with the pastoral team confidentially, ensuring their voices are heard and their needs addressed.
At Boundary Oak, pastoral care is at the heart of everything we do, providing a safe and supportive environment where every child can thrive. Mr Julian Speirs, MA, BEd(Hons) Deputy Head Pastoral
Form Tutors and Tutor Time
In the Junior School, Form Teachers play a key role in pastoral care. As pupils progress to the Senior School, their Form Tutors remain essential, and daily Tutor Time supports well-being through a structured programme covering topics such as bullying and mental health.
Pupils actively share their ideas, thoughts, and concerns, influencing decisions on topics such as lunches, policies, and events through the School Council. _______________________
Prefects take on leadership by chairing meetings, while other pupils can join the Council or become Peer Mentors. _______________________
Reflecting our focus on pastoral care, we also appoint a dedicated Pastoral Ambassador to support and inspire their peers.

pageCache.pageTitle: Senior School Curriculum | Boundary Oak School
pageCache.text:
Senior School curriculum
Small class sizes and strong teacher-pupil relationships underpin the Senior School experience.
The Senior phase is full of academic purpose and exploration of avenues for the future. Your child will enjoy a fulfilling, tailored education that will develop their intellectual curiosity, freedom of thought and expression.
Boundary Oak pupils follow a two-year programme of study in Years 10 and 11 towards GCSEs or IGCSEs. Most pupils will sit exams for between seven to nine GCSE subjects.
Super school, friendly, inclusive, and disciplined. Great sports and after school provision with solid, enjoyable learning and equipping pupils for the future.Senior School Parent
Subjects
All Senior pupils learn the core subjects of maths, English and science.
Pupils enjoy a varied academic progrmme, with co-curricular activities and trips supplementing the curriculum. Each pupil also enjoys five hours of sport per week.
Our teaching staff represent some of the best in their field, and the strong, supportive relationships they build with pupils mean we can expertly guide them through their choices as they enter Upper Senior School.
Lower Seniors - Years 7 and 8
Pupils in Years 7 and 8 study the core subjects of maths, English, science and languages, plus humanities, creative arts, outdoor learning and ample time for sports. Pupils try each of the three languages (Spanish, French and German) during the first term of Year 7, before choosing their preferred language to continue with during their Lower Senior years.
After two years of enjoying the richness and variety of our Senior School timetable, pupils at the end of Year 8 will take forward two subjects from music, drama, art, DT, outdoor learning, food and nutrition or a second language into Year 9.
Upper Seniors - Year 9
In Year 9, our pupils study the broad core subjects of maths, English and science, plus their choice of two subjects from drama, art, music, food, DT, outdoor learning, humanities, and their chosen language.
Year 9s also have rotating courses in finance, entrepreneurship, public speaking and photography (each lasting 8 weeks).
We carefully guide Year 9s to select their GCSE options, ensuring as many opportunities and career paths are open to them as possible.
Upper Seniors - Years 10 and 11
Upper Seniors undertake between 7-10 GCSEs.
Pupils are able to choose from a wide range of GCSE options:
Design and technology
Food preparation & nutrition
Download our GCSE options booklet for more details.

pageCache.pageTitle: Early Years Curriculum | Boundary Oak School
pageCache.text:
Our Early Years curriculum
The Early Years Foundation Stage (EYFS) is taught across Pre-School and Reception at Boundary Oak.
As a through school offering a holistic education from ages 2 to 16, we encourage connections between year groups throughout the school year. Pre-School and Reception classes frequently collaborate on activities, including weekly forest sessions, sports days, and our much-loved annual EYFS Christmas Concert and Pre-School Graduation.
Play-based learning
Children enjoy play-based activities and outdoor learning with their friends in the school’s beautiful grounds.
Careful planning means children feel they are playing freely while gaining knowledge and skills to ensure progression throughout the year.
We start by building fine motor skills through activities such as clay modelling. Children also build gross motor skills by digging, climbing, balancing and mark-making. These foundational skills strengthen young bodies for Pre-Prep.
Pre-School Curriculum
In Little Acorns, we focus on three prime areas of the EYFS curriculum:
We are outdoors as much as possible, using the weather, seasons, and planet to inspire learning.
Children start to receive specialist-led lessons in French, forest school, PE, and music, enriching their classroom learning and sparking curiosity. These sessions are seamlessly woven into our termly seasons and celebrations, creating a dynamic and inspiring educational experience.
Communication and language
Personal, social, and emotional development
Physical development
Forest school
Pupils enjoy the wonders of nature through forest school, a core part of our outdoor learning programme set within our beautiful grounds. Led by specialist forest school leaders, these sessions are child-led and interest-driven, focusing on nature-inspired themes such as foraging, hibernation, or seasonal changes over a six-week period.
Children engage in exciting activities like building dens, identifying bugs, and creating with mark-making and craft tools—all designed to nurture creativity, resilience, and a deep connection to the natural world. Our forest school approach inspires curiosity, collaboration, and confidence, providing pupils with invaluable skills that extend far beyond the classroom.
Curriculum - Reception
We deliver the EYFS curriculum through our Nine Aspirations, basing the curriculum around the children’s interests through fun mini-projects incorporating all areas of the curriculum. Examples include:
Create your own book
Make a model of a tree
Plant and seed
Display an art exhibition
Plan and prepare a picnic with friends
Build and complete an obstacle course
The curriculum in action
Daily phonics sessions in Reception are vibrant, interactive and designed to ignite a love of reading and writing. Using engaging methods like songs, actions and games, children explore the sounds that form the foundation of language.
Outdoor learning
Our Early Years pupils enjoy immersive lessons in a dedicated outdoor space, where learning is shaped by the seasons and the weather.
With a structured curriculum, children explore nature through activities like studying fungi, flora, and fauna, caring for our bees, or embarking on scavenger hunts.
We also enjoy fun, hands-on experiences such as campfire cooking, roasting marshmallows, and creating bug habitats. Collaborating with our Pre-School during these sessions allows the opportunity to share our love for adventure.

pageCache.pageTitle: Arts - Senior School | Boundary Oak School
pageCache.text:
Creative and Performing Arts in the Senior School
Pupils passionate about the arts are in their element at Boundary Oak!
Influential teachers nurture and celebrate talents and interests, encouraging pupils to develop their creativity.
Excellent facilities at the heart of our school include the Acorn Theatre and an art and design studio, significantly enhancing the experience for those studying the arts.
Art
Pupils explore and foster their creative potential at school through mixed media, including fine art, photography, fashion and textiles, ceramics and clay work, pottery, and print-making. Museum and gallery visits, both in the UK and through international trips, help develop their understanding, interpretation and appreciation of the arts.
Pupils with a strong interest in art can extend and develop their learning at clubs within our school’s Enrichment Programme. We also run an inter-house art competition, with the best pieces submitted to national ISA and Globeducate competitions. Excellence in National and Global Competitions
Music
Pupils engage in musical ensembles and performances, festivals, musical theatre productions, orchestral concerts, competitions and performances.
We support individuals in gaining the confidence to make a debut performance at our Teatime Concerts or the skills to take music grading examinations.
As part of our Enrichment Programme, pupils can extend their learning through one of many music-based clubs, such as choir, orchestra, musical theatre, or rock band.
Music lessons
Many of the children learn an instrument with one of our peripatetic music teachers, who are experienced orchestral players, singers and gigging band musicians.
Learning to play an instrument or to sing is not only hugely beneficial to cognitive development and fostering emotional intelligence but also enriches other aspects of school life, helping to shape a well-rounded, confident individual.
Piano/keyboard
Guitar (acoustic, electric, bass, ukulele)
Recorder, flute, clarinet, saxophone
Violin, viola, cello
Music theory
Drama
Our specialist teachers inspire pupils to discover their creative potential and build confidence through a variety of exciting performance opportunities. Whether it’s acting in theatrical productions, delivering powerful public speeches, reciting poetry, or engaging in spirited debates, pupils have the chance to shine in front of an audience.
Behind the scenes, pupils can also explore the world of stage production, with hands-on experience in lighting, sound, costume, and make-up design.
These diverse opportunities not only foster artistic expression but also develop teamwork, leadership, and communication skills, equipping pupils for their future careers and beyond.
Individuals who opt to do additional drama peripatetic lessons can work towards LAMDA qualifications, performing monologues, duologues, or devised theatre – or all three!

Little Acorn's Pre-School
Pre-School at Boundary Oak
Little Acorns is a joyous, caring, and homely Pre-School for children ages 2 years 9 months (rising 3s) to 4.
Your child’s happiness is the key focus for our kind, highly qualified Early Years staff.
We teach through play! Our carefully designed environment fosters a sense of freedom while subtly building essential skills like resilience, fine and gross motor development, and a strong foundation of knowledge.
Curriculum
Children develop a love of learning through a fun, active EYFS curriculum that incorporates sensory stimulation, arts and crafts, bug hunting, tree climbing and other exciting adventures.
Our specialist teachers provide exciting lessons in French, sport, forest school, PE and music, offering children a broad and enriching experience. The children enjoy participating in school plays, and special events like craft afternoons with their families, creating lasting memories together.
Why choose Little Acorn Pre-School at Boundary Oak?
As well as learning among a small class in a homely atmosphere, our play-based Pre-School offers:
Personalised care and teaching
Flexible sessions
Purpose-built facilities
Forest school & outdoor learning
Early Years Funding accepted

Reception at Boundary Oak
Learning through play and exploration
Reception at Boundary Oak is a happy adventure for children aged four to five. Each child is given close personal attention, helping to maximise their educational, personal, and social experience.
As children take their first steps into learning in Reception, we ensure every day is an adventure. There are plenty of opportunities for exploration, hands-on play, songs, laughter and fun alongside sessions that begin to lay the foundations of reading, writing and mathematics.
We provide abundant opportunities to explore the great outdoors to develop children’s confidence and self-esteem through the power of play. Children gain so much as they run, climb, learn, and discover the natural world in our extensive woodland grounds.
The curriculum evolves and deepens as the year progresses, gradually building on key skills and concepts to support children’s growing abilities. Children also benefit from weekly lessons with subject-specialist teachers in music, outdoor learning, French, and PE.
By the end of Reception, most children will have completed the Early Learning Goals and are ready and excited to transition to Pre-Prep.
Boundary Oak bear
Children who join us in Reception are given a Boundary Oak bear and a journal to document their summer adventures prior to starting school. The experiences they document give us insights into what they love so we can tailor their learning to better connect with their interests.
Why choose Boundary Oak for Reception?
As well as learning among a small cohort in and inviting environment, our Reception class offers:
Personalised attention
Flexible wraparound care
Purpose-built facilities
Explorative trips that bring learning to life
Early Years Funding is accepted
Small class sizes
A typical day in Reception
In Reception, children follow a flexible timetable that blends play-led exploration with focused learning opportunities. Daily learning sessions, such as Monster Phonics and Motor Movers, develop key skills in reading, writing, and physical development, seamlessly integrated with time spent with subject specialists. The day begins with registration at 08:35, includes a midday break for lunch and play, and concludes with a heartwarming storytime before hometime at 15:30. A weekly highlight is the visit from Headmistress Sophie Savage, who celebrates the children's achievements with their proud pegs, fostering a sense of accomplishment and joy.

pageCache.pageTitle: Sport - Junior School | Boundary Oak School
pageCache.text:
Sport at Boundary Oak Senior School
Sports are a priority at Boundary Oak, with pupils enjoying five hours of organised sport per week.
We offer a wide range of different sports, so there is something for everyone to enjoy.
Sport for all
A comprehensive schedule of weekly fixtures enables children to experience the joys of teamwork, exercise, and competition. Beyond this, we offer a diverse range of sports-related clubs. Always looking to inspire and motivate our pupils, we regularly welcome international sports stars into school to talk about their experiences and host guest coaching sessions.
Competitive and recreational sports
Competitive sports at Boundary Oak include rugby, football, cricket, hockey, netball, cross-country, swimming, athletics, basketball, badminton, tennis, and dance. Recreational sports include table tennis, fitness, squash, lacrosse, volleyball, and pickleball.
We believe everyone can find joy in sports here. Our inclusive pathway is designed to suit all abilities and interests, with opportunities to participate at all levels.
Sporting events at Boundary Oak

pageCache.pageTitle: Enrichment Programme - Senior School | Boundary Oak School
pageCache.text:
Our Enrichment Programme
A well-developed, comprehensive programme enhances life at Boundary Oak.
We are very proud of our Enrichment Programme offering pupils over 100 after-school clubs, alongside exciting off-site trips and visits.
Central to school life is our House System, where inter-house events and competitions build teamwork and school spirit. The Kindness Counts initiative further enhances our provision by encouraging pupils to make a positive impact. Pupils try new things, discover interests, and gain skills. Being with like-minded peers can mean there’s as much excitement at our debating club as at sports fixtures. We encourage all pupils to explore an interest, get involved and find their place in our supportive community.
Clubs, Trips & Visits
House System & Competitions
Kindness Counts

pageCache.pageTitle: Kindness Counts - Senior School | Boundary Oak School
pageCache.text:
Kindness Counts Campaign
The Kindness Counts campaign embodies our culture of kindness.
Kindness remains a cornerstone of our community ethos, deeply embedded in our PSHE curriculum and daily life.
Our pupils actively engage in purposeful acts of kindness that make a tangible difference, from supporting local initiatives like beach cleaning, recycling drives, and visiting nursing homes to helping new pupils settle by being great buddies. The 'Kindness Counts' campaign fosters leadership and compassion, encouraging pupils to take the initiative and shape their own acts of kindness.
We celebrate these efforts, nurturing a culture where kindness is valued and actively practiced, benefiting both pupils and the wider community. Since 2018, as part of PSHE, staff and pupils have responded to acts of kindness by being kind to someone else.
Below is an example of our wonderful Senior pupils paying it forward.
For more inspiring acts of kindness, follow @boundaryoakschool. #KindnessCounts.
Last year, the whole school took part in the TCS Mini Marathon in support of the WWF, raising over £3,000.
Charity partners
We partner with the charities below because they align with our values and the needs of our school and community.

pageCache.pageTitle: Outdoor Learning - Senior School | Boundary Oak School
pageCache.text:
Outdoor Learning at Boundary Oak
Fostering a love of nature and the outdoors
Senior pupils continue the unique Outdoor Learning Journey to self-discovery that they began in Pre-School.
These journeys are an exciting blend of academia, co-curricular activities, trips, and residentials throughout each pupil's time with us. The entire experience means individuals uncover passions, interests, and desires through various character-building experiences. For Seniors, this also means the opportunity to complete their Duke of Edinburgh's Award.
Duke of Edinburgh’s Award
The DofE is a popular activity for pupils at Boundary Oak. All pupils in Year 9 are encouraged to complete their Bronze DofE. The award is in four parts:
Those who enjoy the Bronze award (or the sense of achievement that comes from completing a challenging expedition) can complete their Silver award in Year 10.
Volunteering
Physical recreation
Expedition
